Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of advanced non-Hodgkin lymphomas and multiple myeloma. However, no CAR-T cell product targeting CD30-expressing malignancies has yet received clinical approval. CD30CAR-T cells generated using viral vectors have shown encouraging clinical activity in Hodgkin lymphoma. Here, we evaluated CD30CAR-T cells produced entirely through locus-specific, non-viral genome editing, an approach that facilitates rapid and multiplex genomic engineering.

Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing, we optimized homology-directed repair templates (HDRTs) and established an all-in-one multiplex editing strategy to knock-in (KI) a CD30CAR transgene into the T-cell receptor α constant (TRAC) locus. The resulting CD30CAR-T cells were evaluated in vitro and in vivo.

We first compared multiple anti-CD30 single-chain variable fragments (scFvs) in CAR constructs containing an FcIg detection domain and CD28/CD3ζ signaling domains. The high-affinity, humanized 5F11 scFv yielded the highest frequency of CAR-positive T-cell expansion. We next replaced the FcIg detection domain with a truncated CD34 (tCD34) detection domain. 5F11-CD30CAR-tCD34-T cells achieved high CAR knock-in efficiencies (approximately 50–80% at days 12–14 after editing) while maintaining potent in vitro activity and therapeutic antitumor efficacy in vivo. We then evaluated multiplex editing by co-electroporating guide RNAs (gRNAs) targeting PDCD1 (PD-1) and B2M (β2M). CD30CAR-β2MKO-T cells retained antitumor functionality and exhibited a low frequency of chromosomal translocations. In contrast, CD30CAR-PD1KO-T cells did not demonstrate improved performance in repeat

antigen-exposure assays. Simultaneous disruption of both PDCD1 and B2M during the same editing step reduced CD30CAR-T cell expansion and resulted in detectable chromosomal translocations.

Non-virally engineered 5F11-CD30CAR-T cells represent a promising therapeutic strategy for CD30-positive lymphomas. While β2M knock-out was feasible without compromising function, PD-1 knockout did not enhance CAR-T cell activity. Moreover, simultaneous PD-1 and β2M disruption increased genomic alterations and chromosomal translocations, highlighting current potential limitations of extensive multiplex genome editing.

"publication_date": "2026-09-02", "description": "

Supplementary data for "OpenScientist: evaluating an open agentic AI co-scientist to accelerate biomedical discovery." This dataset contains research logs, knowledge states, provenance files, and generated figures for seven case studies spanning neurodegenerative disease transcriptomics, multiple myeloma genomics, survival proteomics, drug side effect analysis, and more. Each case study includes the full agent iteration log, configuration, and final report.

Input datasets are included for three case studies where data sharing is permitted: case study 3 (neurofibrillary tangle transcriptomics), case study 4 (multiple myeloma RNA-seq), and case study 6 (drug side effect frequencies from clinical trials). 

Version 2 (August 2026) adds supplementary material for case study 3 (neurofibrillary tangle transcriptomics): 60 additional independent runs of the same question and dataset, comparing three agent/model configurations — Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.8, and the omp harness with Kimi K3 and GLM 5.2 — each run 10 times online and 10 times in a fully air-gapped configuration with no network access and literature served from a local 40-million-article MEDLINE mirror.

Files: ..._supplemental_online_30runs_data.tar.gz and ..._supplemental_airgapped_30runs_data.tar.gz each contain 30 runs with reports (Markdown, PDF, HTML), all generated figures, per-iteration transcripts, the exact prompt, and full version/commit provenance. ..._supplemental_60runs_metrics.csv gives per-run runtime, tool-call counts, literature searches, findings recorded and token usage for all 60 runs.

Version 3 (September 2026) adds two further supplementary sets for case study 3 (neurofibrillary tangle transcriptomics).

..._supplemental_reproducibility_10runs_data.tar.gz contains 10 independent runs of the same question on Claude Opus 4.6, all run on 2026-03-08 with byte-identical inputs (the research question and the input .h5ad were SHA-256 verified identical across all 10) and a 10-iteration budget. Each run includes the report (Markdown, PDF, HTML), knowledge_state.json with structured findings and literature list, per-iteration transcripts, and the job UUID. These runs quantify run-to-run variability under fixed inputs.

..._supplemental_genomic_skill_comparison_data.tar.gz contains 30 runs — 15 using the original genomics Agent Skill and 15 using a revised version — with the two skill definitions included alongside the jobs. The revised skill adds explicit guidance on donor-level pseudobulk aggregation and mixed-effect modelling; the paired arms allow the effect of that guidance on the analysis the agent chooses to be assessed directly. Each run includes reports (Markdown, PDF, HTML), per-iteration provenance transcripts, and container logs.

This record contains processed genomic data supporting the findings of the associated manuscript. Circulating multiple myeloma cells (CMMCs) were enriched from peripheral blood and sequenced using a targeted capture panel. The dataset comprises 55 sequencing libraries from 32 patients across three contributing centers, sampled longitudinally during therapy.

Data are organized as one archive per sequencing library, named by internal library identifier (L#####). The _S## suffix in each filename is a sequencer demultiplexing index and does not correspond to the patient labels (S1-S32) used in the manuscript figures. Use sample_mapping.csv to map library identifiers to figure labels, patient identifiers, and timepoints.

Each archive contains the native somatic-workflow outputs for one sequenced unit: small-variant calls at successive processing stages (raw Mutect2 calls, the variant-filtration output, normalized and merged-caller VCFs, and the final PASS call set, pass.fix.vcf.gz, each with its tabix index); CNVkit copy-number files (bin-level ratios .cnr, segments .cns, called segments .call.cns/.call.tsv, the bin-test output and a scatter plot); Delly structural-variant calls, both unfiltered and filtered (delly.vcf, delly.filter.vcf); and Mutect2's contamination estimate and filtering statistics.

All patient identifiers are pseudonymous and cannot be linked to individuals by recipients.

Machine-readable dataset of multiple myeloma clinical trials registered in mainland China, curated from official NMPA/CDE filings by the China Myeloma Digital Network
(CMDN), an independent non-profit patient advocacy organisation.

This snapshot (2026-09-09) contains 71 trials, 70 of them recruiting, across 554 deduplicated study centres (337 in China, 217 overseas) covering 31 Chinese provincial-level regions. Registry status: 65 CDE-registered, 4 international-registry-only, 1 other-identifier-only, 1 unregistered. Every record carries an archived PDF of the original filing.

International trial registries cover China poorly, and the national registration platform (chinadrugtrials.org.cn) is a search interface with no permanent per-study URL and no machine-readable export. This dataset closes that gap.

Counting conventions matter when quoting figures: trials_total counts every record including terminated studies, while trials_recruiting is the figure that describes what patients can currently join. Centre counts cover recruiting studies only and are computed after institution-name normalisation, so they cannot be reproduced by
deduplicating raw registry text. Read counts from the summary object rather than aggregating records.

Provided as JSON and CSV. Titles and centre names remain in Chinese as filed; no machine translation is applied. Inclusion of a trial is not a recommendation, and presence in this dataset does not imply that international patients can enrol.

Frozen raw RNA-seq count matrix for teaching differential expression analysis,
derived from the MMRF-CoMMpass project (NCI Genomic Data Commons, open-access tier).

Contents: 60,660 genes x 60 bone marrow samples — 30 at diagnosis (primary blood
derived cancer - bone marrow) and 30 at relapse (recurrent blood derived cancer -
bone marrow), one sample per patient, drawn from 844 eligible open-access
expression files.

Upstream processing was performed by the GDC (STAR two-pass alignment, GENCODE v36,
Data Release 46.0); the 'unstranded' column of the STAR-Counts files was used. No
reprocessing from FASTQ or BAM was carried out. Sample selection used balanced
random sampling with seed 42.

Files:
  mm_counts.csv.gz       raw counts, versioned Ensembl gene IDs
  mm_metadata.csv        file_id, case_id, barcode, sample_type, condition
  gene_names.csv.gz      gene_id to gene_name and gene_type mapping
  mm_counts_symbols.csv  counts aggregated by gene symbol (59,427), for iDEP
  mm_metadata_idep.csv   experimental design in iDEP format
  REGISTRO.txt           full provenance, MD5 checksums and DOI

REGISTRO.txt contains everything needed to reconstruct this matrix from the GDC:
data release, filters, random seed and the named list of the 60 source files.

Prepared for a two-day workshop in which the same analysis is run in R
(DESeq2/apeglm) and Python (PyDESeq2) and the results are compared directly
across languages. Workshop materials are in Portuguese.
